headline: Registry scanning moves into Cloud Security with six new pages; an 80 GB image limit is documented
summary_md:
- **Container Registry Scanning** left the data sources book section for **Cloud Security**, gaining a landing page and five new pages covering how scanning works, re-evaluation, supported integrations, third-party connectors and APIs.
- A new **Rules and Policies** hub now sits above the cloud security, cloud workload and base image rule trees — about 45 pages moved down one level and their relative links were repointed.
- Every registry connector page now carries the same limitation: container images above **80 GB** are not guaranteed to scan.
- **Asana** gained a full set of onboarding prerequisites, and **GCP Pub/Sub** now states that storage notifications are not supported.
- 38 Linux kernel support tables added rows for agent content 2420-41253.

highlights.title: Container Registry Scanning moved out of the data sources section into Cloud Security
highlights.detail: The tree moved from configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsiam-data-sources/cloud-posture-and-runtime-security-data-sources to xsiam/cloud-security, so existing bookmarks break; five pages are new and "Registry Components" was deleted outright.

highlights.title: A new Rules and Policies hub reparents about 45 cloud security rule pages
highlights.detail: Cloud security rules and policies, cloud workload policies and rules, and base image rules all moved one level down under xsiam/cloud-security/rules-and-policies, and every relative link into them was rewritten.

highlights.title: Registry scanning is documented as unreliable above 80 GB per image
highlights.detail: The same warning was added to the Docker Hub, Docker V2, GitLab, Harbor, JFrog and Sonatype Nexus connector pages and to both new configure pages.

highlights.title: The Asana connector page gained its onboarding prerequisites
highlights.detail: SaaS Security scans need an Asana service account token created by a Super Admin, and only the Enterprise+ and Legacy Enterprise plans are supported.

highlights.title: GCP Pub/Sub does not support storage notifications
highlights.detail: A new note states this is by design for the Pub/Sub integration.

highlights.title: Base image rules now name their licence requirement
highlights.detail: The page adds a hint that the feature requires Cloud Posture Security, Cloud Runtime Security or Cortex XSIAM Premium.

items.xsiam/cloud-security/container-registry-: New landing page: included with XSIAM Premium, or with the Cloud Posture Security or Cloud Runtime Security add-on.
Documents Initial Scan Configuration (All, Latest Tags, or up to 90 Days Modified) and WildFire upload of unknown files.
New page listing AWS ECR, Azure ACR, Google GAR and OCI Artifact Registry plus six third-party connectors.
New page describing the three phases: discovery, scanning, and evaluation against current threat intelligence.
Re-evaluation covers vulnerability and malware findings only; secrets and compliance findings need a full rescan.
New page: third-party registries onboard via the registry onboarding API, and no public API triggers an on-demand scan.
New page covering agentless scanning of third-party registries, independent of cloud account onboarding.
items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: Deleted with no replacement in the new tree, taking its registry, repository, tag and digest definitions with it.
items.xsiam/cloud-security/rules-and-policies: New hub page separating rules (what to check) from policies (how, where and when they apply).
items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: Adds service account onboarding and advises cutting the default 10-year token lifespan to 90 days.
Adds a note that storage notifications are not supported for the Pub/Sub integration.
Adds the 80 GB limit and repairs a broken reference to the broker VM registry scanner applet page.
items.xsiam/detect-investigate-and-respond-to-: Rewrites the intro to spell out that a paused agent blocks, quarantines and terminates nothing while staying connected.
items.xsiam/cloud-security/rules-and-policies/: Replaces a "See LINK." placeholder with a real link to Create and manage cloud security rules.
Adds a licence hint requiring Cloud Posture Security, Cloud Runtime Security or Cortex XSIAM Premium.
